question.problem:
Consider the orthogonal set $U$ below. By adding a new vector $x=[{x}_{1},\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3},\,{x}_{4}]^{T},$ extend the set so that it forms an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{4}.$ What is the value of $\frac{{x}_{4}}{{x}_{3}}?$

$$
U=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}
$$

current_example.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of ${U}$ as $\mathbf{u}_1,\, \mathbf{u}_2.$ To extend the given set to an orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{R}^3,$ we need to find a third vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275368/assets/0ad599adf71c9f21de96d582d735062c07c81cc91438869c6c07dd7d8c3d19c6.svg) such that

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275368/assets/ead46de94f2e83b54edc37a902aabdcd611896dfddad6eaaa61bd7dea3c76acd.svg)

So, we consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system above and reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns ($1$st and $3$rd). This means $x_2$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get $x_3=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2(0)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-{x}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
